This was kind of funny. I watched the first DVD the day before making fun of the people cause they were acting like the were dying. So the next day I started and I was laying on the floor sweating like crazy feeling like I was going to throw up. Its is a lot harder then I thought and I'm in good shape. summary: By brother bought in and asked me to check it out
text:
Why did my brother want my opinion? I'm a fitness professional from the clinical side of things (working with people coming out of heart surgury or with osteoperosis, etc), but I've also worked with the military and private gyms. I've seen plenty of fitness fads. Insanity has some interesting differences, and is a good fad to add to the fitness library.

First, people are self-paced and perform an exercise within a certain time limit. After a series of exercises is completed, the series is repeated. I rather like that, especially as someone that leads exercises as it helps to simplify things. Not so fit? Well, you'll have fewer reps. More fit? You might over do it, and that perhaps might be the danger so if you're leading this kind of exercise, then make sure to stress form and such to keep THOSE people safe, too. This aspect of the timing is NOT, however, stressed in the program. In fact, typically (and especially in the more advanced workouts), everyone must "keep up". I think an opportunity was missed here, but Insanity it targetting "hard core" people, or people that want to be, or even people that think they are.

Second, having seen plenty of DVD sets for exercises, I think the progression of these is quite good. You get a lot of disks and a lot of workouts, so that might make a difference. Still, I do NOT see a complete beginner who has lived as a couch potato reaching the most advanced disks any time soon. The workout doesn't promice that, and I think if you take each level at the 60 days, then you're well on your way to doing the body good. Basically, this workout has something for all levels. This is actually one of the best reasons to own the set, though I raise my eyebrows at the price tag, especially since most people that get this set will NOT be able to perform more than half of it.

Still, I do have some problems with Insanity.

First, terminology: I see plyometric being bandied about a lot when talking about this workout. While some of the more advanced routines DO have some more strictly plyometric-type movements, plyometrics is not something that CAN really be applied to a AEROBIC workout. That's not their purpose. What's actually happening here is ballistics, which I find fascinating as I STILL run into people that complain about jumping jacks (and in the same conversation clamour for THIS workout).

Second is just my usual nitpicking about exercise fad videos, really. Our host has lots of energy, but suffers what most new exercise leaders do in their first DVDs--their encouraging remarks and pseudo-science talks are really quite horrid (I'd say that nearly every fitness release has this). It's nothing horribly painful, but as a fitness professional I catch it, and wince, and discover wonder again as no one LATCHES onto the misinformation and sues the fitness person. But the disclaimer saves all, I suppose.

As I say, however, Insanity is a decent set to own. I give it 3 stars, relegating it to a nice change of pace to a video exercise library. It DOES include a lot of high impact (literally, now) ballistic exercises, which I like (I find myself laughing when people seem to attribute the INVENTION of these exercises to our host, but he has put them together in a slick package). I might have given this 4 stars, but the talk is a real killer for me and I've SEEN all of this before--I blame the day job.

Ultimately, I'd buy this for my professional library to meet popular demand, but not my personal one. Get this if you train people that are ALREADY very fit because it does have nice variety. Watch this and take notes if you are a fitness professional becuase there ARE some nifty things going on here, namely the arrangement of the exercise routines and the use of time. Everyone else? I recommend borrowing your friend's first.

My exact words to my brother: "It's ok. I like the timing." He and his fiance were devistated, but I applauded the purchase as apart of their over-all desire to get/stay in shape. I wouldn't be doing my job if I turned people OFF of exercise!

text:
I am currently in the 3rd week of Insanity. My husband and I bought this DVD to work out together since we have such different work schedules that finding time to go to the gym together was impossible (our gym is a 30 minute drive away, too, so you need two hours just to get in a one-hour workout there). However, we can easily find 40 minutes in a day to work out in our living room. I wasn't overweight before I started the program--I was on the lower end of my BMI. However, since I was only getting in about one short run and two pilates workouts a week, I wasn't super toned or really in killer shape either. I would rate my fitness before Insanity as 6.5-6.75/10.00. In only 3 weeks of Insanity, I think I can rate myself as a 7.5/10. That's a pretty big difference for only 3 weeks!

What I love most about these workouts, besides getting such a good workout in only 40 minutes, is that you use your own body weight for resistance. No extra weights or kettle bells necessary. As a petite female, huge muscles aren't really my goal. I want to be toned and be able to do a fair amount of pushups, but I'm not going to lift 100 pound weights to get there. I have not experienced any injuries thus far or actually much soreness at all. (I think it's because you work out 6 days a week, so your muscles don't have time to really get tight; a good thing, in my opinion). But I do recommend getting some good shoes, since a lot of the moves are hard on your ankles and knees. I've done several at-home workout programs before, but this is the first time I can remember having to lie on the floor after the workout because I'm soooo tired! I also love that the workouts are so different and have lots of variety. Much better than running on a treadmill. In short, I recommend this program if you're on a tight schedule and have trouble making it to the gym during the week. (I actually canceled my gym membership after just the 2nd day of Insanity.) It's also a great way to kickstart getting back in shape after slacking for awhile. Definitely worth the money.

summary: You can do it- even if you are overweight and out of shape.
text:
I wanted to write a review to comment on the difficulty of the Insanity DVDs. A lot of people have said it's too high-impact, you won't be able to do this if you aren't in great shape, you'll get an injury, etc etc etc. I'm going into my 2nd month, injury free and pain free. I was out of shape and overweight when I started Insanity, and still am (but I'm improving). I actually hadn't truly exercised for MONTHS before jumping into this program. The key to doing these videos if you are struggling with your fitness level or injuries is modification. I modify the heck out of some of these moves. I rarely do any of the jumps, but modify them to teeny tiny jumps, squats, jogging in place (for jumping jacks), etc. I have issues with both knee and back pain so I didn't want to risk injury, but still wanted an awesome work out. And when I modify these DVDs, I get just that. I am covered in sweat at the end but not in pain.

If you know how to modify exercises to your fitness level, you'll be able to do this. Each time I work out I get better and better at the moves and keeping up. Some day I might even be able to do the jumps, but that is probably quite a ways in my future. If you're overweight, out of shape, and worried about injury and DO NOT know how to modify things to still get a good workout, then this might not be for you. Since there are so many excellent, in-depth reviews out there, I figured I'd just provide a list of pros and cons to aid those who are considering insanity.

Pros:

1. Drastically improves cardio performance. The package includes a fit test through which you regularly track your progress. But even without the formal tracking sheet, you'll quickly recognize improvements day-to-day, and if you use a heart rate monitor, you'll find that your heart rate will stay lower and come down faster than it did in the early days.
2. No extra equipment.
3. Great lower body workout--you will build muscle (which, as I'm sure other reviewers have noted, shouldn't scare women away).
4. Shaun T. He seems like a genuinely friendly guy, and he provides solid advice throughout the workouts.

And here's why I only gave 4 stars instead of 5.

Cons:

1. Harsh on your joints. I'm only 28, and I sometimes found myself needing to ice my ankles/knees (I've never had issues with these joints before). I bought inserts for my tennis shoes, and that seemed to help, but this is NOT a workout for someone with preexisting problems.
2. Music. It's horrendous. Recognizing this, the creators have thankfully included a handy "no music" option. Also, if you have the music on, it's difficult to hear the tips Shaun T provides. They should have used the P90x people.
3. Short-changes biceps/back. This is really a function of how difficult it is to involve the pulling muscles without any additional equipment. That said, the stability exercises are enough to make sure you shouldn't lose any muscle from these areas.
4. Shaun T's grammar. With a workout this intense, you don't want any distractions, and constant errors in subject-verb agreement ("hips is down"; "legs is back") make it tough to stay focused.

Overall, I "like" P90x better than Insanity, but part of that is the fact that Insanity is much, much harder. But since you only get better by challenging yourself, it's probably good for P90x aficionados to shake things up from time to time.

These programs can improve self confidence, but can also decrease it if you don't finish the program. To me, that is as important as learning good form.

A good analogy to this would be like taking an advanced college course. You wouldn't take a calculus course without first taking algebra, geometry, etc. If you did, you'd become lost and overwhelmed, with the end result of dropping out of the course. The same thing would apply here. That's why it's important to build up to Insanity by taking a "prerequisite" program first such as P90x, Supreme 90, or equivalent.

Doing this would greatly increase your chances of completing this program, which will not only improve your over all health, but your self-worth as well.

summary: Fantastic program but NOT for the undetermined
text: I believe that losing weight is most peoples goal, but this program requires rigorous determination and discipline because it is downright hard. Its hard work and while I believe you will see results with just following the workout schedule, it wont do much good if you are continuing to eat trash, so you have to be committed to the program AND eating healthier.  Results will always vary, but the workouts are SO intense that I thought I could get away with just watching what I ate, around 1500-1700 calories most of the time, following as much of the recipes I could follow but not leaving my chocolate cravings behind. In 60 days, without skipping one workout or shutting the dvd off early, I only lost 5 pounds. But I lost inches in places I needed too, my thighs, waist and love handles and I started the dvd's at the point where I needed to lose my last 15 pounds, so it's stubborn stubborn weight (in my case). I have had 4 kids, had only run 2 miles at a time at a mediocre pace, quit P90X early, done a bit of Turbo Jam and Chalean Extreme in the year leading up to starting Insanity. So I basically started with only a little cardio endurance, very little muscle and little motivation. I was sore for the first 3 workouts, and the dvds got tougher but it was easier to turn on the program, I set out a time each day (the first 30 days was in the AM before my kids woke up, the last 30 days had to be at night since the dvd's get longer) and found I was mentally committed even when I was sore or lazy. I have 4 kids, I had guilt free pregnancies, and did not try to lose all the weight gained in between each, and my last child turned 1 when I started. I believe anyone with a healthy body can do this, complete it and be proud. I highly suggest purchasing Asylum as soon as you start month 2, I found once I finished Insanity, I continued the workouts but at my own combinations, I was not as motivated because I got bored, I knew what the expect. Asylum took it to another level, so if youre looking to thin out, and then get lean muscle, that's the route to go. I am starting the Insanity Asylum hybrid next week and I couldn't be more excited about my results... am I at my goal weight yet? No, but Im getting there, Im eating WAY better, less on the snacking, less on the sweets and my results are WAY better than when I was just doing Insanity. I DO NOT like working out, but I DO like fitting in clothes I fit in before I had any kids, I do like having some upper arm definition, I do like having abs, and not feeling self conscious in skinny jeans, I am proud to say I am an Insanity graduate. Its worth it, and its even more worth it if you make the lifestyle change nutritionally with it.

This is an awesome work-out!  I'm a runner and usually don't get much out of exercise videos, but Shaun T will kick your ass!  You will sweat to death and feel like you've worked out the next day.  This is definitely a kick-butt workout and I burn almost as many calories doing these videos as I do running. My heart rate generally stays in the 150s and the 160s.  The first month's workouts are great--absolutely no complaints. However, I didn't like the second month's workouts when I first began them and it took me some time to like them. Max Interval Circuit is an excellent, kick-butt workout and Max Interval Plyo is a good workout as well.  I still don't particularly care for Max Cardio Conditioning. A lot of the exercises in this video in particular are boring and done for too long--for example, he does Power Knee for one minute on each side, which I find to be boring and entirely too long for that particular exercise. There are several other exercises that he does for one minute that are too easy and way too boring to be doing for one minute.  I end up substituting moves from the first month during those exercises.  A lot of his moves in the second month would be better served by doing them for 30 seconds rather than one minute. I do not like the Recovery and Max Recovery videos--all they are is boring stretching. I generally run on those days. I would also like to add that it takes a few weeks to actually get the moves down and do them correctly.  Some of the moves are pretty hard to figure out how to do correctly with proper form and I find that I need a mirror to make sure I'm maintaining proper form. There are still some moves that I can't figure out how to do properly and that I can't do all that well.  If you don't perform the moves correctly, you won't feel as worked out and you won't see maximum results.  Some of his moves are just straight crazy (I guess that's why he calls it Insanity!)  :), but once you learn how to do the moves correctly, you will definitely feel the burn.  Overall, though, this is a really good workout, it will you allow you to push yourself physically, and you will definitely see more tone and definition. I would highly recommend it!

I have just completed the entire 63 day program. I am a 41 year old male, 5'9" and 238 when I started on February 29 of this year. I lost 26 lbs overall. I am now 212, and in about 2 weeks (after a vacation) I am going to start the program again. My goal is to get somewhere in the neighborhood of 185. I have a somewhat larger, wider frame so I think this would be about the ideal weight for me.

I didn't follow the meal plan to an exact. I ate very well though. I didn't eat any fast food, except for twice having pizza. I didn't drink any pop. I had maybe 10 beers in the 63 days. I made my meals smaller, healthy, and more frequent.

I thought the workouts were sensational. They are extremely challenging. I think if someone finds them to be easy, then they aren't pushing themselves to do each exercise as thoroughly as they should be. For example, in "high knees" I'm sure almost everyone could lift their knees a bit higher when they are doing the exercise.

Shaun T is a good motivator. He is in fantastic shape and pushes you hard through every workout. After doing each of the routines a few times and knowing each move, I found I rarely had to watch the TV. I did my exercises in a large mirror to watch my form and I could just follow along to the audio.

I find it amusing that he almost always refers to himself in third person as Shaun T. I believe, in the Insane Abs routine during the bicycles without hands where he says "even I have to take a break during this one" is the only time he says "I" and not "Shaun T".

If you have back problems, shoulder, knee, hip or foot injuries, then you should probably avoid this DVD until those issues have been resolved. There is a LOT of jumping, running in place, push-ups and overall body exercises. This isn't a low impact routine.

The toughest part of the program, though, is this: It is 63 days. You get one day off per week. You have to tell yourself those other 6 days that you HAVE to exercise each day. I have Mondays and Tuesdays off, so I chose one of my days off to be my free day.

There were days I didn't want to exercise. I had to make myself go down to my basement and do it. I was so glad when I was done each day, though. It made me feel really good about myself to be dedicated to something and to follow it through to the end. I was drenched with sweat and my heart rate monitor (which I bought from Amazon during week 2) gave me a read out of how many calories I'd burned and what my heart maximums and averages were, which were a good gauge of how hard I was pushing myself.

I look forward to my second round of Insanity starting May 17. I am in better shape now than I've been in years, and I am sure that I will be in even better condition in mid July, and look like a very healthy 42 year old.

Please buy Insanity if you want to make a change in how you look and feel. Just make the decision that you have the mental toughness to dedicate 9 weeks to working hard.

summary: Wow...it hurts so good!  Very tough, but will make you very happy!
text:
I am going to start off sounding like a lot of other reviewers -- I keep myself in good physical condition, with a thoughtful mix of cardio and weight training, working out 4-5 times a week. And I like to work out hard...um, rather I used to think I worked out hard until I did Insanity.

This is a very, very powerful set of workout DVDs. The whole program is well structured, with a balanced mix of plyo (get ready to do TONS of pushups and jumps, and I mean TONS and TONS), intense cardio (the most intense I have ever done, just crazy intense), and deep muscle-building exercises. What I like a lot about Insanity as well is that each workout DVD remains varied enough that you never get bored putting it into the DVD player. The pace is fast, the water breaks are short (30 seconds each after 3 minutes of pushing the hardest you can, and then all over again), and it is all intense enough to keep you fully engaged throughout.

The ad I saw on TV said "on day one, you will be humbled". Hah, that is so absolutely true -- day one, I took the fit test, which left me gasping and crying and realizing that there is a LOT of work to be done, and I was already in better shape than all of my friends! However, even thought the beginning is tough, this program ensures that you will progress, and that you will progress FAST. It is very hard, no doubt about it; it is sometimes outright brutal (that Max Cardio Conditioning DVD is the hardest thing I've ever done), but it always feel very positive throughout, and it genuinely feels like you are working hard to get tangible results.

One thing that I think makes Insanity exceptional is Shaun T. He is a wonderful motivator, and always strikes the perfect balance between pushing you hard and making sure that you listen to your body take enough breaks for your own well-being. Like he says in one of the DVDs: "I don't care if you take ten breaks during this exercise, as long as you keep coming back." Also, he can absolutely do all of this stuff, which in itself is very impressive and gives him total credibility. The crew he has working out with him seems close-knit and have clearly earned their stripes with him, and you can sense their deep respect for his instruction and guidance, along with a sense of ease and fun that permeates the group. You can also see the positive reinforcement he gives his guys throughout the workout. So just watching the people working out on the DVD behind Shaun T is already a very positive experience.

I am in my final week of Insanity, and as for results, all I can say is wow. For me, it went as follows:
- Weeks 1 and 2 were just trying to get acclimated to these crazy workouts, and pushing through as best I could, and praying that one day I would be able to keep up with the pace and actually complete a workout without needing to collapse in a puddle of sweat halfway through.
- Weeks 3 and 4, I could feel my body gain a lot of power and agility already, and my stamina was up dramatically. I could actually do some of the workouts to the end. I felt really good about myself.
- Week 5 (recovery week): felt so good to work on stretching and building muscle. I felt ready for the rest, and eager to go. My body and mind both felt strong, refreshed, and in shape.
- Week 6-7: totally kicked my backside all over again. The workouts go from being 40-45 minutes long to 55 minutes. Not only that, but all the exercises are a lot harder. The warm-ups alone were just demolishing me. However, that is when I really started noticing that I had lost a lot of fat around my midsection. That is also when a lot of the fighting spirit (the "dig deeper" attitude) really kicks in. And it feels awfully good when it does.
- Week 8: and again, things start to feel a little better. These nightmarish switch-kicks are coming fast and fluid now. I think I can do it. Gaining confidence, abs starting to show :)
- Week 9 so far: OMG completely getting trashed again. This final week is just beyond anything. Everything hurts. But everything also feels transformed. When I compare to week 1, I feel like an entirely different person. And I look different, people are commenting on it a lot. As for stairs, or running to catch a train, or lifting my kids and horsing around with them? Never felt easier or more fluid and natural. Insanity is simply improving my quality of life, plain and simple.

Highly recommended -- however, as Shaun T says in one of his ads, this is not for people who make excuses, this is not for people who are lazy. Stick to it, grit your teeth, push through, dig deeper, it is very much worthwhile :)

summary: Review by someone Completely out of Shape
text:
This is program works but it is hard and it hurts.

I am 5'4 and 180 pounds. I wear a large shirt and size 14 pants. I wasn't always like this, I was an avid hiker even worked at Yosemite for a spell. Then a drunk driver hit me and I couldn't work out for almost a year. Now I am in no shape to do the things I love, like hiking and canoeing which make me very unhappy. So let's try this again and maybe writing this review will keep me on it. (FYI My husband was doing it with me and he was only maybe 20 pounds over his ideal body weight. After 2 months he had KILLER abs. and AMAZING ARMS).

Day 3:
It hurts and if you are out of shape like me, impossible to keep up with. But I have a new rule, do at least one of every exercise, no matter how much it hurts or how hard it is. Do at least 1. My shoulder was seriously injured in the accident, but I am forcing myself to do at least one of every style of push-up. It hurts, and I shake but I am doing it. My thighs hate me right now but I feel good. Proud of myself for actually sticking with it for 3 days. For those that are fit, you won't understand that statement, but for us who are out of shape and ashamed it is such an accomplishment to finish 1 workout much less three. I don't feel sluggish, and my spirits are up. The workout is HARD! Very, very hard. You will sweat, you will be gasping for breathe and if you push yourself may feel like you are going to puke. But, if I push myself like I did the first time, I know I will see results fast. My endurance will go up, I can do the things I love, I will be able to fit into my cute clothes, and my confidence will skyrocket.

Day 20:
Wow, has it really been 20 days? Ok, so there were a few days I was just too sore to do the workout. I mean hurt to walk sore. And even though I promised to try every exercise, sometimes I just couldn't finish the video. I have been pushing myself, and pushing myself. When I say I couldn't finish a video it was because I was on the floor, drenched in sweat, and gasping for air. Has it been worth it? YES! Just the other day, my husband out of the blue tells me I look happier and full of energy. And I do feel like I have tons of energy on the days I workout. If I skip a workout, I feel cruddy. Now what y'all really want to know, weight? Well, I decided not to weigh myself for this workout because I would be gaining muscle so instead I have been relying on my clothes to do the talking. All my fat clothes fit properly and some are loose. Prior to this workout, some of my fat clothes were so tight I thought I was going to have to go up a size. Don't have to worry about that now. :) I could be down more but like I said there were some days I just couldn't do it. Well, one goal is down, my confidence is starting to go up.

Day 40:
Well...I had to stop using Insanity, because I found out I am pregnant. So following doctor's advise I have to downgrade to a low impact workout. But, I was getting results so I do recommend the this workout. Remember that those on the video's are in crazy good shape. Modify exercises you can't do or just jog in place. Never stop moving and you will get results no matter what shape you are in. Good Luck!! FYI, it may take longer than you think to really start getting "amazing" results. Just stick with it.

I don't need to repeat the many reviews explaining how terrific Insanity is (they are right). But I thought I'd add a couple of pieces of advice:

1. Preparing for Insanity
These workout DVDs helped me get into good enough shape that Insanity was doable (NOT easy, but doable without puking): Amy Dixon's Breathless Body: The Ultimate Calorie Burn; Paul Katami's A.S.A.P. Hollywood Bootcamp 4x4; Bob Harper: Cardio Conditioning; and Jari Love: Get Extremely Ripped! 1000.
In case you wanted a DVD to help you prepare, I'd pick one or two of these.

2. Calories
The Beachbody website will give you a calorie recommendation. I found that for me--a very short woman--Beachbody's calorie recommendation was way too high. I recommend calculating your calorie needs for a non-workout day by using the BMR/Harris Benedict equation. Ideally, get a heart rate monitor to calculate how many calories you burn doing insanity (I found a big difference between month one and month two). Add the two numbers, subtract 500, and use that. The result was much lower than what Beachbody's website suggested. Using this lower number, I was not hungry and I lost 15 pounds.

Good luck. Insanity really is a terrific program.

summary: A Healthy Young Woman's Review of Insanity
text:

I am now pretty much obsessed with these videos and Shaun T. P90X? Tony's nothing compared to Shaun T. (Tony makes corny jokes and acts as if things are harder than they actually are.)
MAIN POINTS:
1) I usually hate exercise videos. I prefer the gym or the outdoors, and my other DVDs just sit there collecting dust. Insanity is the FIRST thing I've done that's been worth it to "just press play" - you get a BETTER workout than going to the gym, it's compressed into a smaller amount of time, and it's not too easy. Even the warmup is challenging and worth the minutes. (I've been known to turn off videos during the warmup because I was so bored and unchallenged.)
2) Insanity makes you a better athlete all around. It makes everything else seem easier (running, stairmaster, etc). You're working all of your muscles and getting a great cardiovascular workout.
3) Ladies? Want stronger, leaner, toned arms? Do Insanity. It's crazy how much they've changed for me in 8 weeks. Yes, you're going to do pushups--but Shaun does all sorts of different varieties, so you're not just doing 30 regular push-ups. He makes them fun. (For example I like the one where your body is up in a "V" and your hands point toward each other; you do small bends.)
4) Because of Insanity, I've gotten into the habit of working out in the morning (you can run after Insanity if you eat a little something beforehand!), then drinking a protein shake for breakfast (I use vanilla Whey protein, frozen berries and water/ice in a Magic Bullet). I feel so much better, have more energy during the day, eat healthier. It's awesome.
5) Lastly: I've reaped the rewards from Insanity, and I've only been doing it 3-4 times per week!! Yes, that's right.. most weeks 4, once or twice 5, but I've never done the full 6 days (it's hard for me to get up that early sometimes with my staff). I also run a few times each week, but haven't stepped foot in a gym or touched weights. I was already "in shape", and I've seen my body change.
I am stronger, leaner, feel better, and look forward to seeing Shaun T's face every morning. He doesn't say anything unnecessary in the videos, and the order of exercises is interesting and fun.

Buy it today, you will not regret it.

I started working out in January with the Tracy Anderson Mat Routine, which I did for about two months. I started off using only 1 lb weights and worked my way up to 2 lb weights. Then in March I switched to Jillian Michaels No More Trouble Zones and did that for about a month, moving up to 3lb weights. Then I saw an ad for Insanity and decided I needed to do that. I am REALLY glad I started with the other videos!

I have always hated JUMPING (i'm a "need two sports bras" kind of gal) and would skip the jumping jacks on the Jillian Michaels video, plus having virtually no core muscles of any kind is pretty prohibitive to jumping successfully, so that part of the workout has been challenging. However, now in the 8th week I am FINALLY starting to be able to do some comfortably even. I STILL don't have much in the way of core muscles, but it feels like that is also finally starting to change.

At the end of week 4, I blew out my right knee, which had been heading that way for about a week. Fortunately I am trained in a therapeutic method called "sound balancing" that uses tuning forks to do energetic adjustments, and I was actually able to fix myself up enough to get through that. After the recovery week, though, I really needed a whole week off, for a few different reasons, so when I hit the 2nd part of the workout, I was pretty fresh.

This section is really hard. I can't keep up. I still do girl pushups pretty much exclusively in any of the pushup exercises - that said, though, my shoulders are still pretty cut. Some days I just don't have it in me but I make sure I go through it anyway, even if it is kind of half-a*#ed - better to do something than nothing.

I'm happy to say that the day I finish the workout series I will be headed to the beach for a week and for the first time in my life, I will be wearing a bikini! proudly! and I have Insanity to thank for that!

summary: The easiest way to work this hard.
text:
Here's the deal. Whatever your exercise regimen, it doesn't even come close to the insanity workout. I would dare say that THERE IS NO way to shed more sweat and burn more calories in as little time as plyometric activity, and that's essentially what Insanity is. I'm 20, and average activity level, (I did work out plenty before), and I thought I was in shape... I didn't even know what in shape was.

Insanity is all about moving fast, and light, and controlling your body ever step of the way. While p90x has an emphasis on bulking up (I've done both), insanity is straight, dog-tired, cardio six times a week. The moves in this program incorporate many muscle groups at once, the result is COMPLETE BODY-DRAINING exhaustion.

It is not a short cut. it is not easy. And it may be the hardest workout you've ever done, but it will also make you feel the best you've ever felt.

I can't guarantee a complete body transformation in 60 days, but it's a set of a routines you can do for the rest of your life. It will keep you strong, and healthy.

The only thing I can say against it is that the stretching isn't enough, not for the amount you work during this program. So do a few extra minutes of stretching (particularly after) and you'll thank yourself the next day.

It works because it's about making YOU work your a$$ off virtually ever day. If you're lazy, this isn't for you. If you want to change your body, this has got to be one of the "easiest" ways to do it.

To give you some background: I have been overweight for most of my life. In college I lost a substantial amount of weight (around 70#) just from walking to classes. After graduating, I moved across country, took a desk job, and, you guessed it, gained a bunch of weight back. Prior to trying Insanity, I wasn't doing much fitness-wise - just walking and doing some workout DVDs (Turbo Jam) when I felt the urge, but nothing consistent. I'm proof that if you aren't already in good shape before starting Insanity, it can still be done. The most important advice I can give you is to go at your own pace and keep good form - don't be sloppy (you don't want any injuries!). Also, don't get too frustrated if you can't do all of the moves the first time around - you'll get there! Definitely keep track of your progress - for me the results along the way were just the motivation I needed to push play each morning.

summary: Puts all my other workouts to shame
text:
I'm almost done with the Insanity program (Day 58 of 63), and I am happy with my results. I probably didn't have a lot of weight to lose, so I did stay the same throughout, but my abs are visibly flatter. My abs, arms, shoulders, and legs all have more definition, and I am leaner overall. So don't get too caught up in the scale -- if you do the workouts and not blow your diet, you will see results. I didn't follow the diet plan but overall eat a pretty healthy diet and counted my calories and still saw results.

The first month's workouts are around 40 minutes, which break down into a 10-minute warm-up, 5 min stretch, 20 minutes of the real workout, and 5 min cool-down stretch. While that might sound like a lot of stretching, you'll be grateful for it -- trust me. Most of the discs involve 3-4 minutes of intense activity, with 30 seconds of rest in between sets. You get a recovery week in which you do the same workout six times and then start up the second phase. Those workouts are about 55 minutes and are longer with combination moves. It will feel draining at first, but you do get used to it. A lot of the second phase is mental, so just keep pushing through. The program is only 2 months...

A couple of the discs run straight through with no break after the stretch, but don't worry -- not all the exercises are busters. Just go at your own pace in the beginning and watch your form. I managed to do this in an apartment and didn't cause the building to shake -- this comes by watching how you land. Obviously, if you have chronic mechanical issues, you may want to consider modifying or not using this program altogether.

I am definitely a convert when I thought I would quit from boredom, the required dedication, or difficulty. I have run over 10 marathons and twice as many half-marathons, so although I thought I was in shape, this really pushed me to a new level. I look forward to starting another round in a few months and in the meantime I will step up my old workouts because they are not gonna be the same anymore!

summary: BUY IT HERE, NOT AT BEACHBODY
text:
I just spent a few hours of my morning trying to understand the billing process at Beachbody. I have always wanted to try the workout. I have P90X and felt a bit bored with the repetition exercise, and decided it would be a good idea to do the Insanity for a change.

Like most of you, I came to Amazon first (God Bless Amazon) and found it on PRIME. Unfortunately, I hate to admit, my student budget didn't allow me to buy it this month, so I place it on my wish list and moved on. Burden by curiosity, I decided to log on to my computer again and visit the beachbody site, offering an easy 3 payments for the workout. Now that could workout.

I proceeded slowly and inputted all my information, including my credit card number. At the check out, I saw a total of 76.85! That's right, they catch you on the shipping and handling for 24.95. Then the 11.85 tax didn't add up (even when I figured it out it was based on the total amount, including shipping and handling). I decided to wait. So I closed the browser before agreeing to the total amount--it would be much better to buy it at Amazon. Only, at the end of the day, i received an email Thanking Me for my order. It turned out, the moment you put in your billing information, you agree to buy the product, even if you do not click on the purchase button. You also agree to TRY the workout for 30 days before you can cancel it. Shipping is not refundable and you will pay for shipping the dvd's back yourself!

So my easy 3 payments stand thus: 1st= 76.85 (39.95 + 24.95SH + 11.95TAX) + 2nd= 39,95 = 3rd+= 39.95 for a Grand total of 156.75. SO this is the price for the workout in the end. Even Amazon, offering free shipping, does not escape the grand total amount in the end. Call it what you want, but the price is what the price is in THE END.

Anyway, I made peace with that. It is not unusual for companies such as Beachbody to do this. I am just informing you that if you choose to do so in buying the workout, do it at AMAZON. At least you'll have the satisfaction to know they had to share profit with Amazon and returning items is very easy. I have never had a problem with Amazon, and I even began buying food here too. I just feel that it would be nice if they told you exactly what the price was instead of lying about it. If the workout is indeed worth the price, people will buy it. Now that I see the gimmicks, I am leaning towards this being a big SCAM than an actual workout. Shame.

I just hope the workout is worth the money.

UPDATE: NOW FOR A REVIEW ON THE VIDEOS

When reviewing this product, two things come to mind: It Works, and it is NOT MAGIC.

The exercises are intense and you must keep up with it if you want some results. Keeping up with it will inevitably give you results. However, the secret isn't in the exercise, but the diet. If you perform all the exercises, but do not follow the diet recommendations, this program will not work for you. The dietary recommendations are spot on, but following the diet alone, and going for a two hour intense bike riding (or running) will help you loose the same amount of weight and pop those abs out like a charm.

There's some resistance in the workout videos but it is NOTHING compared to its cousin, P90X. If you're looking to loose weight, and can't stand biking, running, or swimming, and a few crunches every other day, this is the exercise for you IF YOU FOLLOW THE DIETARY INSTRUCTIONS. Do INSANITY in the morning and have a few beers with your buddies at night and you'll grow as large and as "healthy" as a killer whale. I have been doing the exercise with two friends and one did just that. I lost 5 lbs in one week (34 yr); Second friend lost 7lbs (26yr); Third friend gain 10 lbs (29yr). Anyone can do some Googling and understand why he gained that weight--it is not mystery.

If you want to Loose weight and have definition, Insanity + DIET is your game, but you HAVE TO BE COMMITTED. If you want to bulk up some muscle NOW, P90X + DIET is your baby. I'm adding two more stars to my review, only because it is a good guide for those who can't bother with creating their own schedule and exercise routine and want results (again, providing they commit to doing ALL the work). I must admit the videos get boring, really fast. Second week I was blasting my IPOD to motivate me. P90X wins for me because I can use the IPHONE APP, listen to my own groove, workout out at the gym, and when I finish each workout the pump is immediate, visible, and the exhaustion you feel is filled with wonderful accomplishment. It hurts, but you do love it. Jumping up and down in my living room in rapid succession isn't my game.

summary: Insanity Worked for Toning but not for Losing Weight
text:
I am a 5'7" 30 year-old woman with an athletic build. I played sports throughout my childhood and adolescence, religiously lifted weights throughout college, and ate just as much as men because I burned so many calories being active. When I started working a full-time job, I only worked out sporadically, sometimes taking a couple months to get back into a workout routine, and kept up my bad eating habits. So in about 10 years, I gained about 40 extra pounds, weighing a total of 170 pounds. I have been dying to try and stick with an exercise program that could melt off the extra weight so that I could get back to my college weight of 130 pounds. So when I saw the Insanity workout on an infomercial a few months ago, I jumped on it right away and stuck with the full 60-day workout program. I weighed myself each week as one way of tracking my progress. I was disappointed every time I looked at the scale. My weight kept flucuating between gaining a few pounds and going back to my weight when I started the program. At the end of the 60 days, I hadn't lost a single pound... I was the same exact weight as when I started.

Although it was extremely disappointing that I had not lost any weight from an intense workout program and eating a lot less than I used to, I did notice a difference in muscle tone in my calves and arms particularly. I look a lot slimmer in photos, which is great. I also feel like I have a lot more energy throughout the day.

I think that a reason why I was not able to lose any pounds from Insanity is because of my body type. The workouts were challenging, but because I used to be super athletic and strong, I was able to keep up with Shaun T. and his crew from the very beginning. After the 60 days were over and I found myself disappointed from not losing any weight, I set Insanity aside and started my own workout routine where I'd alternate lifting weights and running. I'm only a week into my new workout routine, and I'm happy to report that I'm finally losing weight!

I am thankful that the Insanity program kept me on a tight 60-day workout schedule and toned my body, so I do recommend the program to those who need some extra help to get into an exercise routine. I am skeptical, however, about people actually being able to lose weight from it. For me, it didn't give me the serious resistance training my body needed to turn all my fat into muscle.

So I guess to sum up my review of the Insanity program, some body types will get more or better results than other body types, but it's worth trying because you will at least get something out of it whether it's getting toned, losing weight, getting into a regular exercise routine, having more energy, or simply staying healthy. Best of luck!

summary: It works, its tough, and you'll love yourself for doing it
text:
INITIAL REVIEW: Near end of Week 2 and the program has changed me physically already (I am doing Insanity coupled with a weight-lifting routine). It is extremely hard - although I can now complete the warm-ups without stopping, I still can't keep pace with the people on the DVD and have to stop very, very frequently and can't even complete some of the moves more than 2 or 3 times. Actually, there are some moves that I can't even do once without stopping the DVD to catch my breath. I realize I haven't even gotten to the hard part (Week 6 onwards). I am, however, now very inspired to change other things in my life. Knowing that you have to wake up to do an insanely difficult exercise routine every day catalyzes a lot of changes - ranging from what you are willing to eat, how much sleep you need, how many beers you'll have - and how often you'll weigh yourself! Already lost one belt notch and have gotten gasps at change in physique. Will provide more updates. If this program wasn't so hard, it wouldn't be so inspiring. Can you imagine the importance of proving to yourself you can do something you didn't think was possible? That's what I'm going for. This wouldn't work if it was called "Kinda Tough" instead of "Insanity."

UPDATE: Halfway through Week 4. Super inspiring and exciting to be doing this program. Can now get through the warmups almost at the pace of the people on the DVD (during warm up only!) - this is a huge improvement over when I first started, but I still need to stop DVD during the rest of the workout to catch my breath (usually 5-6 times per DVD for 60-90 seconds each). Still there has been progress! Can't believe I wrote in my first update above that "can't even complete some of the moves more than 2 or 3 times" - that's not the case at all anymore. I can do all the moves, albeit much more slowly than the people on the video. Emergence of a six pack starting - or I can at least see where that six pack will be! Resting heart rate has dropped significantly to levels that are considered very athletic for my age group. Although I'm getting more fit, the program feels harder than ever - probably because I was so far from keeping up with the pace during the first few weeks that I wasn't even close to doing the real workout (and still am not). Core muscles developing in a way they have never done before. Please note I am pairing Insanity with lifting (upper body) 2-3 times/week - pretty easy to do because I don't feel these muscles are drained too much by the workout. That may be, in part, because I can't do good enough push ups during Insanity - I just can't keep up aerobically - so my upper body doesn't get the full workout of the people on the DVD. I had been supplementing Insanity with other lower body workouts (weights, running, elliptical) - had to eliminate all of those because leg muscles simply could not recover fast enough. I also throw in yoga 1-2x a week on top of Insanity. The intensity of exercise program is leading to all sorts of other diet/lifestyle changes - simply don't have the same cravings for pasta or pizza or carbs anymore. Actually holding off on meeting some people that I haven't seen for a few weeks so that I can get to the end of the program and see their reactions to my new physique. Have lost about 1.5 belt notches since starting (I began Insanity with a normal BMI so was not expecting to lose a lot of belt notches). Feel much more confident. These workouts are way harder than training for the half marathon. By the way, the women on the DVD seem to outperform the men (e.g., speed, number of reps/exercise), so this is not just a program for the guys :-)

UPDATE: Just started week 6, month 2. Let me just say I had no idea how hard this was going to get in month 2! In month 1, I could workout 4-6 times a week in the evenings after doing Insanity in the AM - its not that I was finding Insanity easy (I could still barely keep up) but I was recovering quickly. Month 1 is what I expected and would have made me happy if it just ended there because it's a serious accomplishment in its own right. Month 2 is completely different. I've never done a workout this hard. I can't believe I got through two days of it. I'm back to stopping the DVD 10-15 times per workout for additional rests. I feel like I need to seriously focus on pre-workout hydration and diet to get through each session. That said, I definitely feel like i'm on route to being in best shape of my life. Note: don't skip recovery week - you'll need it!

UPDATE: Just started week 7, day 1. Recovered enough to start to add my weights and occassional run back into my workout. Only stopped DVD twice on Max Cardio today (which, granted is much easier for me than Max Pylo or Max Cicuit) - but wow! Never thought I would get here! I think for once someone on the DVD took a rest before me!! That said, pre-workout nutrition (and nutrition overall) has become critical. Need to eat and pre-hydrate with Gatorade 45-60 min ahead of workout - no more water or Poweade Zero. Overall I feel 10x better than before, more confident, calmer, higher energy, requiring less sleep, and less coffee. Imagine I've lost about 10 lbs of fat and have gained 15lbs of muscle (I'm not trying to lose weight and am lifting 2x a week in addition to Insanity). I now actively crave this workout. What is most "Insane" about all this? How much I have changed!

UPDATE: Week 8, day 5. First workout without stopping the DVD (Max Circuit)!

UPDATE: Just finished the program today. Feel amazing. Can't believe I've done this. Biggest accomplishment I've had in a while. Didn't stop DVD once in the past week. Just narrowly missed beating Chris on my last Fit Test, although my final scores now beat Tania and Chris's starting scores (which means I'm in better shape than Super Athlete Tania and Chris the Marathoner were when they started Insanity - not bad!). Overall, this has been a wild ride and a great experience. I'm stronger than I've been in a very long time, I have core muscles that I've never had before (I can do the incline sit up bench at the gym at its steepest height *with* a 35 lbs plate now, no problem), and I'm more aerobically fit than I've been since my early 20's. For instance, I have run 7 miles on my Insanity "rest days." My resting heart rate is down about 20 beats per minute and my blood pressure is down 15 points to low/normal. I was on the thin side to begin with, but I've still lost one notch on my belt. I now read exercises that are recommended in men's magazines (like "jump rope for 15 seconds and rest for 45) and they sound like an utter joke. I guess the only thing I'm worried about is what I should do next! Probably Insanity again or Asylum! Thank you, Shaun T. This was awesome. Kinda saved my life.

Insanity works, its as simple as that. Prior to Insanity (31 yr old male) I was about 20 lbs overweight with a nice round tire on my mid-section. I had been doing moderate weight training the last three years had gotten stronger overall but could not lose the "beer gut" even though I did do some cardio.

After completing the program (stopped lifting weights), I lost approximately 17 lbs with a majority of that being in my mid-section. My legs are far more muscular and toned which has helped me run faster and longer. Before Insanity I could barely run an 8 minute mile, now, I can run a sub 7 min mile, and am able to run longer, faster, and harder. (Also for those with plantar fasciitis - which i have - it is a great way to do cardio that will not strain your foot - mine is actually almost healed).

In order to maximize your gains, you have to go as hard as you can. For example, I started the program with my roommate. We were both in decent shape; starting out I was stronger but he was better at cardio. After completing the program, I can run longer and faster than him, I lost more weight, and am still stronger. Why? Because I pushed my self harder than him. How I know, when we did the program we both wore heart rate monitor and when we were done with a DVD, my average heart rate was 10-20 BPMs higher than him and I burned more calories. It sounds corny, but Shaun T's motto of "Dig Deeper" really is the key. You have to push your self to get through those last few reps or seconds. I would recommend using a heart rate monitor to check your progress.

The one draw back is that I have lost overall arm and shoulder strength. Although you do do a great deal of pushups and other arm and shoulder exercise, I found that it does not offset the lack of weight training.

The one Warning I have is if you live in an apartment complex and live above the first floor you may have problems. There is a lot of jumping and other movement exercises that may wake or annoy your neighbors if you have thin floors/ceilings.

summary: Hard? Yes. Boring? Yes. Waste of money? Yes. Don't believe the hype.
text:
So, like many of you here, I watched the infomercial and was inspired. I really thought that Insanity was the fitness program I was looking for. No equipment needed, and look at the results! So, I laid down the cash and bought the program.

I am a fairly active guy who plays hockey and goes biking at least twice a week. I work at a desk job and really enjoy getting out and moving on the weekends. I was hoping that Insanity would really give me an edge and help to build my endurance. The fit test quickly shows you that you're far more out of shape than you think. Disc by disc and day by day, I found it a huge challenge to even get through the "warm ups". So yes, the program IS challenging. I'm not disputing that. Clearly even the pros in the video had a hard time keeping up.

My dispute is that people are paying in the neighborhood of $200 for some guy to tell them to do variations of basic cardio moves at a vigorous pace. That's the only "secret" to Insanity. Do jumping jacks, jogging in place and push ups as hard and fast as you can for 30 minutes straight. The program gets old quick. I could do this all for free. And it's not very practical to use in your living room if you have any loose items on shelves. I got tired of knocking things over and vibrating everything. Also, get ready for rug burn.

At the end of the day, I have more fun and stay motivated to work out harder playing hockey or biking for a few hours on the weekends than I did with insanity. Sure, if you're someone who hates actual activities, needs someone telling them to stay motivated, or are some body building wannabe freak, I'm sure this program is fine. But if you like to compete and have fun, this isn't the program for you. I could not keep it up and sold it off. Too boring and too much money. The infomercial really makes it out to be some hardcore experience. It's just a workout.

To paraphrase "Eastbound and Down" charachter Kenny Powers, " I like to play a real sport, not be the best at exercising! ".

Think twice about this investment. You may as well just make an audio recording of you screaming "PUSH! GO!," and "BUTTKICKS! JUMPING JACKS! HEISMAN! " than buy this. If you're into that, great. But if you like competing and being outside, pass this and go join a club sport or go biking or jogging for free. You'll have way more fun.

summary: Great workout, but probably not for everyone
text:
Anyone reading this has probably seen the infomercial and researched this enough to get an idea of what it is. It is a high intensity program that focuses on cardio. It is very hard, even if you are in shape to, to get through. In the base set there is no weight or resistance component to it (aside from lots and lots of push ups, and some triceps dips). All the resistance moves come using your own body weight.

Pros:

1) No equipment needed aside from a good pair of shoes, and maybe some floor mats. You do not need dumbbells, a chin up bar or anything else. You do want to have or get a good pair of cross training shoes though. A lot of people wear running shoes doing this, and have lots of issues with pain or twisting their ankles. Running shoes are good for landing, but not plyometrics. They do not have the lateral stability to hold up when doing repetitive plyo exercises.

2) The workouts are relatively short. In month 1 they are all under 45 min, and in month 2 they are all under an hour.

3) The 60 day duration. I have done p90x and doing the same workouts for that long a time just gets boring. This is the perfect amount of time for a DVD workout series to last, and then you can decide to either re-do it or move on to another one be it P90x, P90x2 (also a 90 day workouts but has different workouts in each month) or Insanity Asylum.

3) You cannot outgrow it. As you get in better shape you can go faster and take less breaks so it should never get easy.

Cons:

1) This is not really a program for beginners. Even the people in the videos have a hard time keeping up and have to stop and take breaks. If you have never worked out before or have gotten out of shape after a long layoff, I would suggest easing your way into this. Yes you can do the moves slower and take more breaks when you first start out, but there is really no way to modify the moves to make them easier like you can with other programs.

2) It is very high impact. You are jumping and doing a lot of side to side movements in every workout, so if you have knee and/or back issues this is probably not the workout for you.

3) If you like to lift weights you will probably need to sub out either the recovery workout day or the rest day to do some upper body lifting. With all the squats and jumping you will be doing in Insanity you will probably not have to do much of a leg workout, but for people who can't go without lifting Insanity itself may not be enough.

On Amazon, the price. $144 is way too much, and I have heard about some of the "third party" sellers selling faked bootlegged copies. If you are going to purchase on Amazon make sure it is being fulfilled by beachbody which is the actual company that makes it.

Ultimately the best workout for you is going to be the one that you can stick with. Insanity is a good, but hard program that works if you do it. Like any workout, how well your results will be are going to depend not only on doing the workouts as hard as you can, but also in large part to how you eat. Insanity does have a good nutrition guide to use as a base, but you may need to adjust your caloric intake to get the best results (and for many people that means eating more calories because the workouts are so intense). The main thing is you have to be following some kind of nutrition plan because if you are eating like crap, or on the other end of the spectrum not eating enough, the program will not give you anything like the results of the people in the infomercial.

What you will get is a 13 DVD set that comes with a diet plan and a workout calendar in a pretty good quality case. I Don't know if the free T-Shirt will be available for those purchasing via Amazon.

Anyway, this is my first week on the program and I will say that this workout is totally INSANE! Just the first DVD (Fitness Test) alone, beat every ounce of energy out of my now out-of-shape body. For someone who grew up fairly athletic, I found myself gasping for air in less than 10 minutes into it. Shaun T works out all muscles, core and most importantly, cardio with easy to follow step-by-step, day-by-day instructions. He continually pushes you to keep going and YOU WILL FEEL THE PAIN, but also stresses you not to exceed your max limit, risking injury. I was able to keep up with the routines for so long. I was barely able keep up with his students for that matter. My heart said yes, but my body, of course, said no. I kept pushing and pushing. My heart was racing, muscles raging and knees buckling. It really was HELL!

With that said, this program is not for everyone. I believe it requires one to be in the right frame of mind. Nevertheless, once you choose to proceed and if you are not built like Shaun T or in excellent shape, It is highly suggested that beginners start the exercises at half speed. You will enjoy it more, working your way up to par. I will say that I had a good time struggling through it so far and will continue on for 7 more back breaking weeks to achieve the results I am longing for.

GOOD LUCK and ENJOY!

summary: Hardcore, but not for beginners and a little unbalanced
text:
My perspective: I'm a 25-year-old male who began Insanity as an intermediate-advanced athlete with more than years of boxing/Must Thai training under my belt.

Pros:

Insanity workouts are no joke and perfectly reminescent of the Thai workouts we used to do at my old Kickboxing gym. Pop squats, jump squats, push-ups, etc. These workouts will definitely turn you into a beast.

The pace is great and pushes you to the limit.

I always felt motivated. For the most part.

Cons:

The warm-up is inadequate and could potentially lead to injury.

The exercises are tough but by month 2, you've seen everything Shawn T has to offer. The lack of variety in exercises--everything is some damn form of a squat--will not only strain your motivation in time, but leave you frustrated from diminished returns.

The biggest caveat: this program is not for beginners. If you don't have a base of athletic training, you will not benefit from this program. As someone who's used to doing 2-a-days--training twice a day--with sprints and rounds of pad-work, I still found myself struggling at certain points.

All-in-all, Insanity has kept me in shape but it's a little unbalanced and unrealistic.

Despite this I was actually really looking forward to my next workout, the "Plyometric Cardio Circuit". I was thinking in my head that the fit test would probably be one of the most difficult things in the videos. Also, my blood pressure has dropped significantly since I last I had it checked a month ago, when i was registering a 135 over 85ish. These results could not have been accomplished without Shaun T's videos. And honestly, I enjoy doing them. When I go to bed every night I look forward to doing the next workout the following day. I should also mention that I am on a tough diet. I do not follow the nutrition guide, but instead eat five meals a day, typically involving protein shakes, fruit, chicken, tuna sandwiches, milk, and water. summary: The program works wonderfully - a few helpful tips from me.
text:
For my 40th birthday in October I promised myself a 6 pack. I've always been in pretty good shape, and I've never had one. I started Insanity in early June.

I'm one week from finishing and my results have been very impressive. I didn't lose a ton of weight, but then I didn't have a ton to lose in the first place. I am 6'3", and was 205 when I started and I'd guess around 25 lbs from a 6 pack (small belly, small amounts of excess fat in many places). So far, I've lost 7 lbs overall. I'd also estimate I added at least 7 or 8 lbs of muscle.

I haven't been in this good shape since I was in college 20 years ago. I don't have the visual 6 pack, but I have a 6 pack. My abs are STRONG. I love how it feels. My arms have a ton of sexy definition now while avoiding that "meathead" look I so despise. My quads are huge, and my calf's have mini-calfs on them. Posture is better, self-confidence is through the roof.

So, back to my goal. I have a week left in the program and I know I won't get my 6 pack by then. That's ok. I'm going to take 2 weeks off doing only light exercise and let my body recover. After that I will continue on at a lighter pace, incorporating some strength training at the gym, running/swimming/biking, and maybe 2-3 insanity workouts a week. I have over 2 months left. I will get there.

So, some things I have learned while doing this.

1. Use the BeachBody message boards!! I can't stress enough how important it was for me to go there for support, questions, nutrition issues, etc. I would have failed without the support of my BB coach and others.
2. Take pictures. Take measurements. If you don't. You will get frustrated with your progress, or what you will think is a lack of progress. When you compare your 1st month pictures with your start pictures though, you will have the drive to finish.
3. Buy joint support. I had joint pain even with elbow/wrist/knee braces. (and yes, my form was solid, I'm just 40 years old and creaky).
4. Proper nutrition is 75% of it. If you think you can continue to eat the same old crap that made you fat and exercise it off. BZZZZT. Wrong. If you aren't ready to make solid nutrtional choices, you will not see decent results. Making solid choices takes hours and hours of preparation weekly. Planning. Shopping. Cooking. In my opinion, this program is too damn hard to fail because you didn't eat right.
5. You have to *WANT* it. This program is HARD HARD HARD. You will think of 100 excuses daily to skip the workout. When you start month 2, you will think of 200 excuses daily. You ignore them all and push play anyway. If you don't have the drive to be in great shape, are weak willed, or quit things frequently, do not waste your money. However, If you want overall fitness more than anything else in your life, or want that 6 pack more than your own desert island, this is the program for you.

GOOD LUCK!!!

Good luck and stick with it ... it is the real deal.

summary: Insanity for Women: Practical Advice from a Veteran
text:
I am an athletic female who gains muscle easily and was trying to avoid the "bulky" look that I achieved so easily in sports and working with a personal trainer. I tried Crossfit but was immediately turned off by the overly muscular and judgmental women who said stuff like "she's skinny fat" and "don't you want to look like us?" No. No I do not want to have man shoulders and a body that I define as "bulky" (even if you think bulky = body builder, which it does not!).

If you're in a similar situation to me, then you will LOVE insanity. I was skeptical at first after hating P-90X (not enough cardio, too much shoulder work). Several friends suggested Insanity for me because I 1. Love cardio but hate running, 2. Work crazy hours and so needed something I could do from home, and 3. Like to have something challenging with fast results.

I absolutely love Insanity. It's like it was made for me. I love Shaun T (great motivator) and from a vanity perspective I liked that the women in the videos still looked like women. I completed all 60 days of Insanity and now I basically alternate between the "max" and "regular" videos each morning and take 1-2 days off/week. I started the videos at 25% body fat and am now at 18% body fat which was my goal. I lost 7 pounds and my clothes fit more loosely. I tried to post a before and after link but Amazon deleted it. If you want to see my before and after pic go to pinterest dot com slash sandcastle2 and check out my "fitness" board.

Here is some practical advice for women (and men) about using the videos and things to watch out for:

General: If you are out of shape, obese, or generally hate to exercise, don't do these videos. I'm not sure why this isn't clear to people. But this is challenging. It's still challenging for me and it always will be because you determine how many reps you do and how quickly you go. If you are completely out of shape you will likely get discouraged in the first two weeks, so be prepared.

I do Insanity in my basement on workout mats on top of carpet. I tried it once on hardwood floor and will never do that again (it's high impact). Our basement stays a cool 62 degrees year-round (live in NorCal). I tried this in my parent's house in Texas in 80 degrees and I nearly gave myself heat stroke. I strongly recommend doing this in front of a fan if you don't have AC or naturally cool weather. Keep water nearby at all times and a towel (you WILL sweat). Give yourself at least an hour of cool down time after the workout.

I find that none of the stretches Shaun T. leads you through involve enough back stretching. I have a bad back, mostly upper and some lower, so I tend to pause the stretch and do an extra 2 minutes of back stretching.

As a woman I have been unable to complete all of the "real" push ups (push up jacks, v-push ups, moving push ups in particular). Instead, I do most of these with my knees down and occasionally do regular push ups. I have built incredible strength and muscle tone this way, so it's OK to do "girly" push ups.

Diet: I am a vegan (don't hate) and so I did not follow the nutrition guide. I eat a lot of beans for protein and some soy. I find on days that I did not have enough sugar (fruit) I was unable to complete these work outs. Everyone is different, just be safe and listen to your bodies. I had a buddy who tried to do these videos on paleo and could never finish. Find a balance with your sugar because you do need it for energy. I drank Kaeng Raeng shakes instead of Shakeology after my work outs because I preferred the taste and the high fiber content.

Video-specific advice:

Plyometric: This is essentially the "first" video of the series after the fit test. In the second interval, there's "basketball drills" where you squat down and "jump from the bottom." Do NOT bend over as you will hurt your back, but instead squat down fully (it's harder but correct).
In that same interval are "ski abs" and "in and out" abs. If you are not strong enough in the arms, you will find "in and out" abs nearly impossible. I alternate between in and out abs and doing crunches instead.

Cardio Power: In the second interval you will do "globe jumps" where you squat down and move side to side and back. This is another exercise where it's tempting to cheat. If you bend over to touch the floor instead of squat down your lower back will hurt for a week. In that same interval there's moving push ups. I was never able to do these so instead I either do moving plank or regular push ups.

Cardio Recovery (First): After doing this video I was basically unable to do any Insanity for 3-4 days. I tried it a few times, but every time it would kill my quads so bad I couldn't go up and down stairs. That's not really my style so I skipped this video and did yoga instead. I'm sure it's great for building strength but I found it too debilitating to incorporate regularly.

Pure Cardio: This video involves about 15 minutes of non-stop exercise (no breaks) but Shaun T encourages you to take a break when you need it. The first several times you do this video you likely won't make it all the way through. Don't worry - you're not alone! It took me a full month before I could do all 15 minutes without stopping. At the end of the video there are push up jacks which I struggle with. I, instead, do normal push ups or push ups with my knees down.

Cardio Core and Balance: This is the "off week" video. I did it once and found it too slow and boring so I just went right into the max videos.

Cardio Abs: Frankly this is the weakest part about Insanity. I substitute P-90X's ab-ripper X instead.

Max Interval Circuit: In most of the max interval warm ups, the last exercise is "side to side hops" where you have your arms down and hop your legs from side to side. I have found, for some reason, that this is way too high impact for my quads. Perhaps I am not strong enough in the arms, but I do floor runs instead.

Similarly, in the max interval warm ups are "side to side jump rope." Don't watch the people in the video because it will totally throw off your rhythm and make those impossible.

In the second interval you do "floor switch kicks." These are intended for ab work but if your arms aren't strong enough you likely won't get the ab benefit. I alternate between regular kicks and the jumping switch kicks to give my arms a rest.

Max Interval Plyo: The beginning of this video is quite a lot of leg work, so I was only able to do about ½ of the "squat push ups" at a time. It's so tempting to do these exercises incorrectly to make it easier on yourself but you'll regret it later. In the second interval you do power push ups where you jump in and out of push ups. For some reason I never got good at those and so I do regular push ups.

In the last interval you do these side push ups where you put your hands at a 90 degree angle and kick your legs out to the side. The first time I tried this I hurt my wrist, so I've resorted to doing regular push ups instead for similar results. The same thing goes for the side burpees - I just do regular burpees instead.

Max Cardio Conditioning: This is definitely less high intensity interval and more "can you work out for 45 minutes straight without a break?" I really enjoy this workout on days when I don't want to do the high intensity stuff.

Max Sports Training: This is one of the better videos for your "off" days. Still will get you into a sweat, but not the cardio from the other videos. There is no stretch at the beginning of this (not sure why) so I like to pause it after the "warm up" and do my own stretching before continuing on.

All in all I have had an incredibly positive experience with Insanity. I put the videos on my iPad and take it with me when I travel. I'll do Insanity in hotel gyms and people always come up to me and ask what I'm doing. I've basically memorized the videos at this point, but it's nice to have Shaun T motivating you. I tend to wear dry fit Lululemon clothing and Reebok flex (light weight) shoes. My biggest complaint about the program is how often I have to do laundry because of how sweaty my workout clothes get! A great problem to have 

text:
I am a 39 year old married mom of 3 and grad student. For reference I'm 5'4 and 175 lbs (ouch!) gain muscle easy, am proportioned evenly(I gain and lose weight evenly on my body), have had small back issues, nothing major, knee can hurt due to my weight. I have been doing some sort of exercise for the last year to try to get back to a healthy weight and finally mentally checked in and committed to a better life. I have plantar fascitis in my rt foot and am not superbly fit, although I used to be so I know how to exercise. If you have NEVER exercised in your life then I think this might be too much, especially trying to learn proper form with the moves. If you are out of shape, like me, and have experience with working out, then you can definitely do these videos. But like other people have said YOU MUST have the right mentality. These dvds are ridiculously hard, like cussing at your tv, wanting to cry and vomit hard, but if you do them at your level and maintain proper form you can get a crazy good workout that gives results. You have to want it, so if you don't like to sweat or push yourself or endure discomfort this is not for you. Get some good shoes for stability and ladies: a good sports bra like Enell (I'm a 36DD and this bra is AWEOME). I have noticed that the exercises help strengthen my calfs and have helped my PF. This is high impact but you can modify the routine to fit your needs. I find that I am motivated by the intensity of the workout and make sure to stop when I need to and drink plenty of water. After having completed the P90X program, I was looking to increase stamina as well as further define my muscles. So far, what I am noticing is a lack of variety in the moves that will most likely lead to the "plateauing" that a program like P90X manages to avoid. I'm not into getting rich quick or losing weight quick. I wanted a challenging, sustainable workout, with intense cardio, more complex resistance training and good stretching. Instead, I got:

1) Repetition ad nauseam/Lack of any substantial instruction: a guy repeating himself in an admixture of motivational military/sports cliches ("You can do this"-- "Four more times"--"Faster"-- "push it") in a continuous loop. He's still telling me to push it while I'm drinking water on a break (is he confused?). If the monotony of Sean T.'s "motivation" doesn't make you want to play dance music over top of it, there is lots of joint destruction to distract you with little to no resistance training. I got that I was supposed to "lift with my core" the first hundred times you said it. Can we move on to different advice now or just turn your voice off? What's worse, doing something faster when you don't have a demonstration of the form can lead to injury that much more quickly. Are the people in the video fake screaming because they're pretending they're struggling? Maybe they're just slipping a disk-- jury's still out on that one.

3)Lack of variety: I'm beginning to realize that this is not sustainable simply because it will not offer me enough resistance training.
It's suicides, Heisman, double Heisman, some kind of mummy moves and squat jacks with some pushups thrown in there like salt on a hard-boiled egg-- in every single disc! summary: Insanity...tis an apt title for this program
text:
To preface this review, I'll tell you a bit about myself (it is a workout program, after all). I'm 27 years old, and in average shape. Prior to starting this program, I was doing some light exercise daily (sit-ups, crunches, etc.). None of that even comes close to challenging me like this program.

In a word, Insanity is BRUTAL. I dare say anyone who first picks this up--regardless of previous fitness regimens--will be wiped out. The Fit Test alone is enough to make my body wail in agony. I've only been doing it for two days, but if the pace is consistent, then this will definitely show results.

Imagine this: four exercise drills, each extremely taxing, for a full minute. That's four minutes of non-stop, EXTREME stress on your body. Then, you get a 30 second break, and then it's another four minutes of pain. Now, imagine doing that for 40 minutes each day. Even the warm-up/cooldown stretches are more strenuous than I am used to. That's Insanity (at least thus far).

We all know there are a number of weight loss and fitness programs out there. I've never bought into the "3 minutes a day for the best shape of your life" claims. Insanity makes sense because it is simple: you work yourself to the limit and beyond every single day, and your body grows stronger because of it. And I don't know about anyone else, but I've never heard of anyone not getting results after going to the limit every day over an extended period.

A word of caution, in case it wasn't clear: Insanity is HARD. Listen to the other reviewers when they say that you won't make it through all of the exercises when you first start out. Don't get discouraged. After all: no pain, no gain, right? Do the Fit Test, and I guarantee you'll be convinced that this program will work if you stick to it.

On a side note, Insanity isn't about building muscle, from what I've seen. You'll be burning fat and getting in better shape thanks to the intense cardio.
