summary: Meh. Not worth it, some potential danger, inadequate in many areas
text:
Pros:

1. Shaun T is motivational, and doesn't come across as arrogant as Tony Horton. P90X and P90X2 are much better programs, but I think I'd probably break the screen if I had to listen to Tony for 90 days. I tolerate him only in very limited quantities, maybe once a week or so. ShaunT is OK, although yelling Yo! and talking about himself in third person (Even ShaunT needs a break) is mildly annoying sometimes.

2. It does improve cardiovascular fitness.

3. I suppose if you have weight to lose, it would contribute to wait loss. Can't tell from personal experience since I am on maintenance diet and do not wish to lose weight.

4. Eye candy. There are several guys with nice bodies. Women however in most cases do not have much of a muscle definition and have really puny arms. That should have given me a clue that this one is not really for me.

Cons:

1. Insignificant upper body work. I've added upper body training twice a week and additional yoga once a week, but that is just enough not to experience deterioration, I am not making any more progress with my pullups and advanced pushups (backclap for example, or hands on medicine ball, feet of stability ball pushups).

2. Workout is rather imbalanced, can result in too strong quads and consequently tight calfs, hamstrings, and IT band. I am adding additional exercises to correct this, additional stretches and also some foam roller work.

3. Risk of injury - so far haven't injured myself, but I've been doing plyometrics moves in other workouts for years. However, a friend who just started injured himself on Day 1, fit test. Knee injury, it will take weeks to recover.

4. Stretching is inadequate. Shaun T is obviously not flexible enough, and stretches are too easy and incomplete. I normally add my own stretching.

5. If you are already fit starting this, you can't expect big progress, except maybe in exercises you don;t do that often. My first fit test was: switch kicks 123, power jacks 60, power knees 75, power jumps 69, globe jumps 12, suicide jumps 21, push up jacks 36, low plank obliques 76. My second fit test was: Switch kicks 108, power jacks 53, power knees 91, power jumps 82, globe jumps 11, suicide jumps 23, pushup jacks 40, low plank oblique 86.

6. Squats are too shallow. Even in recovery workout, when you are supposed to do "slow deep squats" they are not slow and you do not go below the position of thighs parallel to the floor. Insufficient challenge for gluteus muscles. Same applies to those leg lifts and kicks in plank position - I normally do these with added ankle weights, doing it bodyweight doesn't do anything for me. If you want a strength workout for legs and core, Butts&guts from Cathe works great.

7. Not enough variety with pushups. Too simple, no advanced pushups.

8. Core exercises not challenging enough. If you can do swimmers pushup with 2 medicine balls in P90X2,or pushups on 3-4 medicine balls, anything you encounter in Insanity will simply not be enough. Also I normally do twists with my feet up entire time + 6 to 9 kg resistance (depends how many reps), so bodyweight twists just do nothing for me. Ab Ripper from P90X and P90X2 is much better, and so is STS Abs od Cathe. There should be also something added for low back. Supermens for example.

9. Price is just not worth it. Especially considering that there are so many good programs which are free, for example www.lovingfit.com.

There are no weights or equipment to buy. Just have a towel, a bottle of water, and motivation to look and feel awesome.

Some of the negative reviews on here seem to be short-sighted, and I feel the need to address some of their issues:

-"Not for Beginners": This all depends on your level of motivation because, as it is flashes across the screen and as Shawn T reminds you during the program: "Go at your own pace, but push yourself." I spent a lot of time in the gym and rucking (walking with a ruck sack on my back) in Afghanistan and then took 6 weeks off and did nothing when I got back. While I could lift weights, I was NOT in any sort of shape when it came to cardio, so I was back to being a beginner in that respect. At 7 weeks into the program (at the time of this review), I am doing pretty great with keeping up with the cardio now.

-Joint Problems/Injuries: There is a lot of impact in this program due to the jumping exercises. HOWEVER, there are things you can do to minimize this, like substituting the jumping for lunges, squats, calf raises, butt lifts, or any other leg-intensive exercises that they show you how to do during the 9 weeks. Take some supplements like Glucosamine/Chondroitin and Omega-3. Do the static running exercises on a mat or do the exercises in a room with carpet and padding. Do NOT do this program on concrete.

-No Results: If someone said they did this program and didn't get any results, then they're either lying or were shoveling fast food into their face. Like all weight loss programs, you still have to watch what you eat. The good thing about this program is that it is structured and is easy for you to plan out HOW and WHEN to eat based on the level of exercise. There is even an eating guide if you don't know how to properly diet.

summary: Yes, the workout is intense but I LOVE it
text:
I am three weeks into the Insanity program and I can't rate the product highly enough. Does it work? I think so.

I hadn't consistently worked out since the beginning of the year due to work, family, and other commitments (I know -- excuses, excuses!). So I needed a workout routine with a 'defined' timeline (even if ambitious) that would keep me motivated. Insanity has fit the bill perfectly. Shaun T is a good instructor and I personally enjoy his training style on the DVDs. And the '60 day' schedule feels doable.

Below are my observations / suggestions three weeks into the program --

1) Be ready for a challenge. As many others have noted, the Insanity workout program is intense. If you are not used to intense cardio / interval training (or MAX interval training), it takes getting used to. The first week I thought I was going to collapse and found myself cursing at the TV on several occasions.

2) Get a heart rate monitor. If you try to keep up with the exercises, your heart rate will be elevated. It's important to ensure you are staying safe. Doesn't mean you don't push yourself. The first week my heart rate was 100% or more of the 'theoretical' maximum for someone with my profile.

3) Invest in a workout recovery formula (NOT necessarily the recommended brands) -- I already had the whey protein, casein, multi-vitamins, etc (all from Optimum Nutrition). but I was skeptical of the BeachBody endorsed 'Results and Recovery Formula'. I experimented without a recovery formula for the first few days, and found that I was drained for several hours after the workout, and then extremely sore the following day. Rather than get the BeachBody formula (it is expensive!), I decided to try the Optimum Nutrition 2:1:1 mix (Mucho Mango), and the difference was phenomenal. I had more energy after the workouts and wasn't as sore the following day despite pushing myself further in subsequent workouts. This is NOT an endorsement for any particular brand. Get what works for you but IMHO a workout recovery mix is important. Some people say chocolate milk works just as well. I haven't tried it.

4) Stay aware of what your body is telling you and ADJUST. This workout can be tough on your joints, especially knees. I don't have knee issues, but I invested in knee braces because on some days my knees would hurt and I would have to ice them.

5) Try and stick with the program. Did I mention this workout is intense? Some days you will feel your muscles are sore, or your knees hurt, or you are lacking motivation. As Shaun T says, "just push play". Once the warm up routine starts, you'll get into the program.

Again, these are just my observations. As of now, I am seeing results and am motivated enough to push through the rest of the program. 5 stars!

I've tried so many other videos in the past but can never keep up with them for more than a few days because they're BORING! Insanity surprised the heck out of me. First of all, there's a schedule which means there are several different videos that rotate during the week (6 days on, 1 day of rest) which helped a lot with keeping me entertained. Second, I was too tired to be bored! These videos kept me dripping sweat and gasping for breath. I also loved how they didn't feel scripted. The instructor, Shaun T., doesn't seem to be entirely relying on cue cards and the folks working out with him, not only do they take breaks but even better, they don't have fake smiles on their faces the whole time! What a relief! It's scary seeing a whole room full of people grinning from ear to ear while they supposedly push themselves to the limit. Luckily, this doesn't happen in Insanity, not at all. I don't measure my body and I don't use a scale, but I can see the changes in the mirror and in the fit of my clothes. I haven't changed my diet AT ALL, and I haven't completely followed the program (admittedly I've skipped some days), but I am still seeing great results. Insanity is set up to give you a nice, lean, toned body. It's not going to give you bulging pectorals or massive biceps, but you will feel stronger, more energetic, and you will lose weight. Also, I am very impressed with all of the Team Beach Body products as a whole. I have purchased P90X and Chalean Extreme and although I have not done them yet (still too into Insanity), they also look great and I'm excited to try them out.

summary: Ignorance is no Bliss -- with Insanity
text:
PROFILE: 42 yrs, 6'2" 233 lbs

Before exercise/before Insanity:

Went for a routine med check up & after examination (blood work included) was diagnosed as hypertensive, Cholesterol level normal, but HDL (good cholesterol) was subnormal. Translation: Risk candidate for heart disease. And that's not to mention with the high BP I was also at risk of getting TIA(Transient Ischemic attack/Stroke). My glucose level was normal, but my HbA1c, or glycohemoglobin test was subnormal. Translation: Risk candidate for diabetes.
You can imagine how one feels with this new realization. I was depressed beyond words. But somewhere in the depth of my soul a part of me screamed "I want to live!!!!!"

And so began my journey...

EXERCISE:

Now every individual's height has a correlating weight range. For me @ 6'2" mine is about 180 lbs - 190 lbs (you can Google yours up). Below that, I'm underweight, above that, I'm overweight. So, this range gives you a "comfort zone" to bounce up & down in, weight-wise.

But I weighed 233 lbs. 40 lbs above my expected upper limit.

I hit the gym for about 4 months. For 2 months not much happened. But through trial & error, I understood,rather than work 30 min on the elliptical, I stepped it up to an hour with 10-15 min resistance training (weights, dumbbells etc). My weight dropped from 233 lbs to 217 lbs. Then it steadied there. Meaning my body had found a way to adapt to what I was doing. So with a slight change in diet (oatmeal + yogurt for breakfast only, for 1 week -- every other thing constant) & I switched to biking (13 miles) twice a week on our local bike trail/lane I dropped to 200 lbs. Wow, I told myself, good job. But again my body began to adapt & my weight steadied. Besides the weight problem, my love handles hung round my waist like an unwanted belt.

INSANITY:

We all see the infomercials. Yeah, I was like they (all gimmicky health ads)promise so much but will they deliver? Then a voice from over my shoulder (my wife) said: "Why not call & place an order?" And so I did. That was on the last week in Sept. This is my journey so far .....

I came into this with a lot of swagger and confidence. After all, I'm the dude who bikes 13 miles, right? What could this Shaun T fella possibly throw at me that I couldn't handle?

Ignorance, in this case, turned out not to be bliss...

Began Insanity on Mon. Oct 1st. Liked the coincidence in chronology, but HATED day 1 fitness test. 10 min (ONLY) & I'm already gasping like a drowning man. Correction: I was GULPING air.
By week 2 Thursday, I almost gave up. YES, I wanted to quit. What rubbish was this? My body ached, I was beyond sore and disgruntled. I mean it was ABSOLUTE madness. OK, I can now see where the name came from. But, I also realized my mind & body were in their final collision mode. A war of mind over matter. One had to give for the other. I literally WILLED myself through (an 1 hr and a half later FOR A 45 MIN WORKOUT). But once I over came what I believed was the last fabric of resistance by my body; I knew I'd pull through to the end.

Week 3: Tuesday: My "Aha, eureka" moment.

For the 1st time since I began this private boot camp, I finished it without having to pause (YES, I ADMIT IT!) the video. Initially, the 30 sec breaks were too small for me, and I was taking 3 min breaks by pausing it. But this Tuesday, I did none of that, and watched myself pull through without a single pause. Finally, the wheels of stamina had begun to slowly turn...

Today, Oct 18: did Cardio Recovery & I notice that my body isn't aching like in the previous weeks. Definitely, something is happening. Something wonderful.

Will update this piece as I continue to count down.

After I had a baby I wanted to get back into shape ASAP. I ordered Insanity and the results are looking great so far. I have completed one month of the program and noticed a big difference. This reminds me of military bootcamp all over again and I love it. If you haven't purchased it yet, do so.

summary: If You're  Already Fit, This May Not Yield the Results You're Looking For
text:
First off, let me just say, YES, I have completed the 60 days. I am writing this post based on 60 full days of Insanity.

A short back-story because I think it'll help. I have been doing distance running for a number of years now, and completed the Boston Marathon back in April. Along with a rigorous running regimen, I also go to the gym three times a week to strength train. Additionally, I will usually use my elliptical machine at least twice a week. On any given day, I work out for between 1.5 to 2 hours. That said, you wouldn't look at me and see that I'm ripped, however, I am lean and I am very physically fit.

I started Insanity in my running off-season, because it's hot here and I was getting burned out on running. I wanted to replace running as an experiment and see if I could condition myself in other ways. I wanted a workout which would be hard and challenge me, as well as lose a few pounds and get more "cut". Enter Insanity.

When I started the first month's workouts, I really felt like they weren't long enough (about 35 minutes), so I decided to run 4 miles prior to doing the videos every day. The first month was somewhat challenging; however, I was very disappointed in the lack of calories I was burning. Although Insanity follows the HIIT protocol, I could not get my heart rate above 160 bpm no matter how hard I tried. Perhaps this has something to do with my current conditioning. After month 1, no weight loss, no definition. Nada.

After month one, I was a bit frustrated because I was seeing 0 results. I read that month two was much harder and that is where people supposedly get the most results. Awesome! Bring it on, I thought. Month two is hard (VERY); however, here are my issues with it:
- Intervals are short (3 minutes), I barely got to 160 bpm, and then I was back into recovery mode. Though the workouts were longer, I was still not yielding the calorie loss that I hoped. On average, during a 55 minute workout I would maybe burn up to 350 calories.
- WAY TOO MUCH jumping, I noticed my knees were getting jacked up (and this is coming from a runner who averaged 50 miles per week of running and never had knee problems).
- WAY TOO MANY push-ups. I could care less about my chest muscles, I have breasts covering them up, after all.
- Work outs were random and didn't offer balanced conditioning.
- Cast members really started to annoy me, especially Tania (don't ask why, I could write a whole blog post on these people alone).

After month two completed 0 RESULTS! In fact, I gained 2-3 pounds (please note that my diet did not change at all during this process, the only thing that changed was the fact that I was not running nearly as much). WTF?!?! I did a before and after photo, and I swear I must have bulked up or something, because I actually look worse. I've concluded that I have crappy genetics (actually, I concluded this when I was about four years old, but this only further validates it). I will never get "cut". I have been ten pounds lighter than I am now, and still was never cut. I think this is also proven by some of the Cast Members on Insanity. Take Akeel (misspell?) for instance. This dude is ripped like Shaun, however, he can barely make it through many of the intervals. I noticed that I almost always out performed him. Also, look at the various people in the video; they all vary greatly in how much they are "ripped". If you work out a ton, and are not ripped, like me, then you got dealt the crappy genetics card (thanks mom).

My overall analysis is if you're fit, you may see marginal results, depends on your genetics. If you're lean, be prepared to get a bit "bulky". If you're a runner, you're better off sticking with running and do some strength training on your off days, plus, you won't risk killing your knees in the process. That said, I will continue to do Insanity a couple times a week, because I feel it does have some redeeming qualities; however, just didn't yield the results I expected.
